title: TestFlight
objectives: Understand TestFlight via a real-life analogy
Automate uploads + tester invites via API + Fastlane pilot
Manage build expiration + beta app review
Fit TestFlight into a mobile release pipeline

sections.markdown:
**Think of TestFlight as Apple's built-in beta-tester delivery system — the iOS equivalent of Play Closed / Open testing.**

Unlike Firebase App Distribution (ad-hoc IPA + email invite), TestFlight is Apple-hosted, uses the same App Store install mechanism, supports auto-updates, and reaches up to 10K external testers per app.

- **Internal testers** — up to 100 App Store Connect users with team roles. No review; instant delivery.
- **External testers** — up to 10K by email or public link. First submission needs Beta App Review (~1 day); subsequent updates are auto-approved unless major changes.
- **Build expires after 90 days** — testers can't install after; you must re-upload.
- **iOS + iPadOS + macOS + tvOS + watchOS + visionOS** — TestFlight covers all Apple platforms.
- **Tester feedback + crash reports** — TestFlight app collects them.
- **Automatic updates** — testers get new builds automatically if opted in.

**From a DevOps view:** TestFlight replaces Firebase App Distribution for iOS external beta. TF External is the wide-beta ring; TF Internal + Firebase App Distribution split internal duties. Automation via Fastlane pilot + App Store Connect API is smooth.

**TestFlight** is Apple's beta distribution service integrated with App Store Connect. Supports **Internal Testing** (up to 100 App Store Connect team members, no review, instant) + **External Testing** (up to 10K by email/link, ~1-day Beta App Review on first submission, auto-approved thereafter). Builds expire after 90 days. Delivered via native TestFlight iOS/iPadOS/macOS app. Cross-platform for all Apple ecosystems.

sections.code:
platform :ios do
  lane :testflight do
    api_key = app_store_connect_api_key(
      key_id: ENV['ASC_API_KEY_ID'],
      issuer_id: ENV['ASC_API_ISSUER_ID'],
      key_content: ENV['ASC_API_KEY_CONTENT'],
      is_key_content_base64: true,
    )

    match(type: 'appstore', readonly: true)

    Dir.chdir('../..') do
      sh('flutter build ipa --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols')
    end

    pilot(
      api_key: api_key,
      ipa: '../build/ios/ipa/Runner.ipa',
      # Distribute externally:
      distribute_external: true,
      groups: ['beta-testers', 'partners'],
      # Beta App Review info (only on first submission or major changes):
      beta_app_review_info: {
        contact_email: 'release@example.com',
        demo_account_name: ENV['DEMO_ACCOUNT'],
        demo_account_password: ENV['DEMO_PASSWORD'],
        notes: 'Sign in with demo account for full feature access.',
      },
      changelog: changelog_from_git_commits(pretty: '- %s', number_of_commits: 20),
      # Skip waiting — pilot returns immediately after upload; review happens async:
      skip_waiting_for_build_processing: true,
      # Optional: prompt reviewers about specific new content
      beta_app_feedback_email: 'feedback@example.com',
    )

    upload_symbols_to_crashlytics(dsym_path: '../build/ios/ipa/Runner.app.dSYM.zip')
    slack(message: 'iOS TestFlight build shipped 🚀', channel: '#releases')
  end
end

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: Reusing build numbers.** Apple rejects duplicate `CFBundleVersion` on upload.
**Mistake 2: 90-day expiry surprise.** Old builds expire → testers can't install. Re-upload regularly.
**Mistake 3: External submission without demo account.** Reviewer can't test → rejected.
**Mistake 4: Encryption compliance skipped.** Apple asks about encryption; wrong answer → review delay.
**Mistake 5: Broad External group as 'internal'.** External requires Beta App Review; use Internal for team.
**Mistake 6: No changelog.** Testers ignore anonymous builds; use `changelog_from_git_commits`.
**Mistake 7: Ad-hoc IPA via App Distribution when TestFlight is available.** TF has better UX + auto-updates + wider reach.
**Mistake 8: Signing / provisioning-profile mismatch.** IPA fails upload validation.
## Best practices
**1. Auto-bump build number per push.**
**2. Auto-generate changelog from git.**
**3. Demo account credentials in review notes.**
**4. Encryption compliance answered.**
**5. dSYM upload to Crashlytics.**
**6. Re-upload before 90-day expiry.**
**7. Internal for dev team; External for beta.**
**8. Public link for open beta programs.**
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Upload IPA to TestFlight Internal via Fastlane pilot.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — External group + Beta App Review notes.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — Changelog + Slack notification on upload.

**Practice 5 (Hard)** — Automated re-upload before 90-day expiry via Cron.
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — Multi-platform TestFlight (iOS + macOS + tvOS) release pipeline.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Internal vs External TestFlight testers — differences?**

**A:** **Internal testers** — must be added as App Store Connect users with a role (Admin, App Manager, Developer, Marketing, Sales). Up to 100 per app. Any build uploaded → available instantly to Internal testers (no Beta App Review). Great for dev team + close QA. **External testers** — up to 10K by email or public URL. First submission requires **Beta App Review** (~1 day, human reviewer at Apple checks the build meets guidelines-lite). Subsequent updates auto-approved unless major changes. Great for beta cohorts + external partners. **Groups:** you can split External testers into groups + distribute specific builds to specific groups. **Public link:** generate a URL; anyone can join (up to 10K cap). **Interviewer signal:** knowing the 100 vs 10K + review-vs-no-review distinction.

**Q2: What does Beta App Review check + how do you avoid rejections?**

**A:** **Beta App Review** is lighter than App Store review but still checks: (1) **Crashes / stability** — build must not crash on first launch or in obvious flows. (2) **App Store Guidelines Lite** — no obvious violations (fraud, spam, IP violations). (3) **Demo account works** — reviewer must be able to reach main features. (4) **Encryption compliance** — properly declared. (5) **No obvious placeholders** — 'Lorem ipsum' or 'coming soon' screens. **Avoid rejections by:** (1) Testing on real device before submission. (2) Providing demo account credentials + comprehensive notes. (3) Answering encryption compliance question correctly. (4) Auto-bumping build number. (5) Uploading dSYMs. **Only the FIRST external submission per version is reviewed** — updates are auto-approved unless major changes (new features requiring re-review). Interviewer signal: knowing it's lighter + how to sail through.

**Q3: What's the 90-day build expiry + how do you handle it?**

**A:** TestFlight builds expire **90 days after upload**. Testers can't install expired builds; existing installs continue to work but users can't re-download. **Handle:** re-upload every 60-70 days OR every push to your `main` branch (frequent uploads inherently avoid expiry). **Automation:** CI cron job that checks expiry via App Store Connect API + triggers a re-upload if the current TestFlight build is within N days of expiring. **Alternative:** always deliver from tags — every release tag builds + uploads → constant refresh. **Notification:** ASC emails you 7 days before expiry. **Trap:** vacation / holiday → expiry hits → external testers can't install → user complaints. **Interview red flag:** not knowing about the 90-day rule at all.

**Q4: TestFlight vs Firebase App Distribution — when do you use each?**

**A:** **TestFlight strengths:** (1) Apple-hosted; official channel. (2) Up to 10K external testers with public link. (3) Auto-updates for opted-in testers. (4) Better UX (native TestFlight app; users know it). (5) Cross-platform (iOS + iPadOS + macOS + tvOS + watchOS + visionOS). (6) Same install path as App Store. **Firebase App Distribution strengths:** (1) No review at all. (2) Faster upload → install (no processing wait). (3) Cross-Firebase project ecosystem. (4) Ad-hoc distribution outside Apple's review. **Best pattern:** use BOTH. Firebase App Distribution for the innermost ring (every push → QA); TestFlight Internal for the dev team's next ring; TestFlight External for wider external beta. Interviewer signal: knowing both fit different rings, not either/or.

**Q5: How would you architect an iOS release pipeline using TestFlight?**

**A:** **(1) Every push to `main`:** CI builds → uploads dSYMs → distributes to Firebase App Distribution qa. **(2) Nightly:** builds → uploads to TestFlight Internal (whole dev team). **(3) Weekly (Friday):** builds → uploads to TestFlight External beta group (invited beta users). **(4) Release candidate (tag `v*-rc*`):** uploads to TestFlight Internal for last-mile QA + TestFlight External for release-eng smoke test. **(5) Production (tag `v*`):** uploads to TestFlight External (mirror for support debugging) + submits for App Store review + phased release on approval. **(6) All builds:** dSYM upload + Slack notify. **(7) Auto-bump build number per upload.** **(8) `changelog_from_git_commits`** in every submission. **(9) Every 60 days:** cron re-uploads latest build to prevent expiry. **(10) Match + ASC API key + rotate quarterly.** Interviewer signal: end-to-end rings + automation.

**Q6: How do you handle TestFlight for enterprise / regulated apps?**

**A:** **Enterprise:** Apple Enterprise Program (paid $299/year) lets you distribute IN-HOUSE outside TestFlight/App Store — but strictly employee-only. Misuse (distributing to non-employees) = revocation. TestFlight better for most cases. **Regulated (pharma, banking, health):** (1) Auditable release process — GitHub Actions + protected branches + code review. (2) Regulator-approved change log (auto-generated + reviewer-attested). (3) Signed commits via GPG + protected release branches. (4) External beta needs additional consent flow for regulated data. (5) Retention of every build + audit logs. (6) Compliance-specific certifications (SOC 2, HIPAA) require documented CI/CD process. **Multi-region:** iOS App Store rules differ by country (e.g., China needs a Chinese-territory MOU); test-flight allows beta before submission. **Interviewer signal:** knowing enterprise vs regulated compliance nuance.

## Real-world usage

- **Every iOS beta program.**
- **Public beta of consumer apps.**
- **Feature validation with real users.**
- **Cross-platform Apple (visionOS, macOS, tvOS).**
- **NOT for** — ultra-private enterprise (Apple Enterprise Program).

## Advanced notes

- **Public link** — invite anyone up to the 10K cap.
- **`pilot` action** — Fastlane's TestFlight uploader.
- **`change_notes` in ASC API** — auto-populated changelog.
- **Bugsnag / Instabug** — richer feedback than TestFlight's built-in.
- **Tester feedback** — screenshots + text via TestFlight app.
- **In-app feedback prompts** — TestFlight surfaces them.
- **Crash reports in TestFlight** — mirror Crashlytics.
- **Public URL cap** — 10K per public group.
- **Sub-groups** — organize testers by cohort.
- **App Store Connect API TestFlight endpoints** — full automation.
- **Xcode Cloud + TestFlight** — deep integration.
- **App-Specific Passwords (legacy)** — 2FA workaround; deprecated in favor of API keys.
